analysis.title: 2027 US Equity Outlook: The beginning of the middle
key_insights: GS forecasts the S&P 500 at 8,700 by year-end 2027, a total return of about 18% including a 1% dividend yield (the cover page rounds the price gain to 17%). That compares with a 21% annualized return over the past four years.

S&P 500 EPS growth is forecast to slow from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027 excluding mega-cap tech 'other income' from private investment stakes. On a headline basis the 2027 growth rate is 11%, and growth should slow further in 2028.

The forward P/E fell 19% in 2026 and sits near its 10-year average of about 18x. GS expects elevated interest rates and AI uncertainty to hold it there, so earnings rather than multiple expansion drive 2027 returns.

AI capex drives about half of S&P 500 EPS growth in 2026. The contribution shrinks in 2027 as capex growth slows and depreciation builds, and the net impulse turns negative in 2028 even if spending keeps rising.

The 8,700 target uses an 18x multiple on haircut consensus 2028 earnings. GS's 2027 EPS forecast is close to consensus, but its 2028 forecast is about 7% below consensus, and it assumes consensus 2028 estimates converge to GS's during 2028.
The biggest downside risk is a worse 2028 earnings outlook. Each $50 billion of AI capex or 1 pp of semiconductor profit margin in 2028 moves S&P 500 EPS growth by about 1 pp.

Downside scenario: consensus EPS falls back to the 30-year trend and the P/E falls to 17x, which takes the S&P 500 down about 25% to roughly 5,600. Upside scenario: investors gain confidence in consensus 2028 EPS and the P/E rises to 19x, which gives 9,400 (+27% from the 11/17/2026 level).

Earnings growth is concentrated. The top 10 contributors account for about 2/3 of consensus S&P 500 EPS growth in 2027, and NVDA alone for nearly 25%. AI infrastructure stocks have supplied nearly 50% of the index return since late 2022.

Enterprise AI adoption is early. In Q3 2026, 13% of S&P 500 firms quantified AI productivity on a specific use case and 3% quantified the earnings effect. GS expects the earnings impact to become clearer in 2027.

GS flags late-bull-market dynamics: a Fed hiking cycle expected to run through early 2027, AI spending that relies on external financing, and net US equity supply rising in 2027 by the most since 2000. It also notes there is no speculative mania, and that elevated dispersion and improving breadth favor stock pickers.

Theme 1, the AI relay race: the best returns for AI infrastructure stocks are behind us as hyperscaler capex growth slows from 105% in 2026 to 73% in 2027. Leadership should move to monetization and adoption beneficiaries, including the hyperscalers.

AI infrastructure and semiconductor prices imply a substantial EPS decline, which sets a low bar for a short-term bounce. Semiconductor earnings and margins are above trend, so GS does not expect sustained outperformance without visibility on 2028 and later earnings.

Hyperscalers: cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT rose from about 24% in Q1 2024 to 54% in Q3 2026, and announced backlogs total $1.8 trillion. The four largest trade at 22x forward EPS against a 10-year median of 28x. Slowing capex is positive only if the cause is not weaker demand.

For AI productivity, GS recommends companies with a large physical presence, which lowers disruption risk. A screen of 38 non-technology Russell 1000 stocks (Exhibit 50) has traded roughly sideways for two years, matching the equal-weight index. Software strength is concentrated in cybersecurity and IT infrastructure.

Theme 2, the great re-leveraging: hyperscaler capex exceeded operating cash flow in Q3 and consensus has free cash flow falling further in 2027. The S&P 500 buyback yield is 1.4%, the lowest in two decades outside recessions. GS expects 'buyback aristocrats' (Exhibit 51) to outperform, especially if growth slows.

Theme 3, value in growth: positive but decelerating growth has historically favored momentum, EPS revisions, quality, Info Tech and Health Care. Valuation dispersion is at a 10-year low and the Growth factor ranks in the 11th percentile of the past decade, which supports Growth over Value.

Energy infrastructure is a rare area of accelerating 2027 earnings despite an expected decline in energy prices. Transports are an attractive cyclical exposure if energy-price and interest-rate pressures ease more than GS expects.

Theme 4, safety in diversification: Health Care and Consumer Staples earn modestly below trend and trade at undemanding multiples on trend earnings. They have been negatively correlated with the AI trade and outperformed after past overextended bull markets. GS analysts favor biopharma, parts of managed care, beauty, energy drinks and nicotine.
Mid-caps look cheap. The S&P 400 trades at a forward P/E of 14x and 16x trend earnings, and its earnings sit slightly below trend while S&P 500 earnings run well above the 30-year trend.

sector_views.rationale: Capex growth and revisions are slowing, and the best returns are seen as behind. Semiconductor margins and earnings sit above trend, although prices already imply a sharp EPS decline.
Cloud revenue growth is accelerating, backlogs total $1.8 trillion, valuations have derated, and slowing capex is positive for free cash flow if demand holds.
Rare earnings acceleration in 2027 from secular investment in energy production, transportation and storage, even with lower energy prices expected.
Attractive cyclical exposure for the macro upside scenario. Transports have recently lagged other energy-sensitive cyclicals.
Earnings are below trend, the multiple on trend earnings is undemanding, and the sector is inversely correlated with the AI trade. Analysts favor biopharma and parts of managed care.
Earnings are below trend, the sector trades at a discount on trend earnings and diversifies AI exposure. Analysts see the most opportunity in beauty, energy drinks and nicotine.
Forward P/E of 14x and 16x on trend earnings, both large discounts to the S&P 500, with earnings slightly below trend.

earnings_insights: GS S&P 500 EPS forecast (estimate, not a print): $415 for 2027 (+11%) and $460 for 2028 (+11%), against $375 for 2026 (+36%). Excluding mega-cap tech 'other income' from equity stakes, 2027 growth is 18% and 2026 growth is roughly 30%.
GS 2027 EPS is similar to consensus. GS 2028 EPS is about 7% below consensus, and GS assumes consensus 2028 estimates move partway to GS's over the next 12 months.
Consensus (not GS) has the top 10 contributors accounting for 2/3 of S&P 500 EPS growth in 2027. NVDA is nearly 25%, and Exhibit 12 lists MU, GOOGL, AVGO, AMZN, MSFT, AMD, MRK, GILD and SNDK.

Q3 2026 earnings season, reported calls: roughly half of S&P 500 firms discussed AI productivity, 13% quantified a use-case impact and 3% quantified an earnings impact. Examples quantifying an earnings impact include BR, CHRW, NOW and YUM.
Hyperscaler free cash flow is forecast by consensus to decline further in 2027 and rebound in 2028. Hyperscaler capex exceeded cash flow from operations in Q3 2026 (reported).
Hyperscaler 2027 EPS contribution scenarios from GS: +13pp upside, +9pp baseline, -3pp downside. In 2028 they are -1pp, -5pp and -9pp.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS economists see growth close to trend. Lower energy prices support real consumer income, while tighter financial conditions and a smaller fiscal boost offset part of it.

macro_indicators.reading: Hiking cycle under way, expected to continue through early 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: A Fed hiking cycle coincides with the AI boom's reliance on external financing, which GS lists among late-bull-market dynamics.

macro_indicators.indicator: US IG and HY corporate debt issuance
macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from $2.4 trillion in 2026 as AI investment leans on external financing.
Down 19% in 2026 and near the 10-year average. The cyclically-adjusted P/E is 38x (90th percentile).
Lowest in two decades outside recessions, as capex has crowded out buybacks.
GS commodity strategists expect lower energy prices, which support consumer income. Energy infrastructure earnings should still grow.

trade_ideas.description: Own hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT) as the next leg of the AI trade after infrastructure
trade_ideas.rationale: Cloud revenue growth has accelerated, backlogs total $1.8 trillion, capex growth is decelerating and valuations have derated.
trade_ideas.risk: Slowing capex driven by weaker demand rather than discipline would not be positive.

trade_ideas.description: Own physically-intensive AI productivity candidates, the 38-stock Exhibit 50 basket (GM, KO, CVX, XOM, UPS, CSX, DAL, DUK and others)
trade_ideas.rationale: Large physical presence reduces AI disruption risk while the companies have discussed productivity gains on earnings calls.
trade_ideas.risk: Dispersion will stay elevated as investors sort AI winners from AI-disrupted companies, and the basket has only matched the market for two years.

trade_ideas.description: Own 'buyback aristocrats', the Exhibit 51 basket of S&P 500 stocks with consistent share repurchases
trade_ideas.rationale: Investors should reward strong free cash flow and cash returns, and the group has done best when growth decelerates. It trades at about a 2% P/E premium to the equal-weight index.

trade_ideas.description: Own Growth as a factor, plus Energy infrastructure for earnings acceleration
trade_ideas.rationale: Decelerating earnings favor secular growth, accelerating earnings and upward revisions. Valuation dispersion is tight and the Growth factor is in the 11th percentile of the past decade.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower energy prices expected by GS commodity strategists.

trade_ideas.description: Own Transports as a cyclical exposure to the macro upside scenario
trade_ideas.rationale: Transports have lagged other energy-sensitive cyclicals, and would gain if energy-price and interest-rate pressures ease more than expected.
trade_ideas.risk: Cyclicals have generally lagged in positive but decelerating growth environments.

trade_ideas.description: Diversify with Health Care (biopharma, parts of managed care) and Consumer Staples (beauty, energy drinks, nicotine), and own mid-caps
trade_ideas.rationale: Both sectors earn below trend, trade at undemanding multiples on trend earnings, and are inversely correlated with the AI trade. Mid-caps trade at 14x forward earnings and are not over-earning.

risk_factors: A deteriorating 2028 earnings outlook is the biggest downside risk to 2027 equities.
AI capex in 2028 is uncertain, and rising semiconductor supply threatens profit margins and earnings.
S&P 500 earnings run about 25% above trend because of the AI investment boom, and valuations on trend earnings are near record highs.
Late-bull-market dynamics are present: a Fed hiking cycle, AI spending reliant on external financing, and rising net equity supply.
Hyperscalers carry roughly $3 trillion of lease and unconditional purchase commitments, and consensus free cash flow is falling in 2027.
AI adoption could disrupt existing revenue streams, business moats and the labor market, although GS economists expect limited labor disruption in 2027.
Earnings growth is highly concentrated in a handful of stocks, with NVDA alone nearly 25% of 2027 consensus EPS growth.
Fiscal policy is likely to provide a smaller boost in 2027, and financial conditions have recently tightened.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 labels GS S&P 500 EPS at $375 for 2026 (+36%), $415 for 2027 (+11%) and $460 for 2028 (+11%), with a year-end 2027 price of 8,700.
Exhibit 7 labels the S&P 500 12-month forward P/E at 18x (71st percentile) and the cyclically-adjusted P/E at 38x (90th percentile).

Exhibit 10 gives hyperscaler capex scenarios. Upside is $1,700B in 2027 (+92%) and $2,000B in 2028 (+18%), baseline is $1,529B (+73%) and $1,619B (+6%), and downside is $1,000B (+13%) and $750B (-25%). 2026 is $884B (+105%) in all three.
Exhibit 18 labels 77 US IPOs in 2026 YTD against a post-2000 median of 105, with 394 in 1999 and 268 in 2021.
Exhibit 25 shows year/year cloud revenue growth for AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT rising from 24% in Q1 2024 to 54% in Q3 2026.
Exhibit 21 is titled to say AI infrastructure stocks have given back much of their 2026 gains in recent weeks.
vol_and_positioning: Return dispersion is very elevated, valuation dispersion across S&P 500 companies is at a 10-year low, and market breadth is improving. GS says this favors stock pickers.
Concentration is high. The weight of Information Technology and Communication Services in the S&P 500 is at a record, and AI infrastructure stocks drove nearly 50% of index returns since late 2022.
Net US equity supply, including expiring lockups, is forecast to rise in 2027 by the most since 2000. Only 77 US IPOs have launched in 2026, against a 25-year median of 105.
AI infrastructure stocks have given back much of their 2026 gains in recent weeks, and semiconductor prices imply a decline in future EPS.

tension_points.bull_case: Emerging AI productivity gains, a stronger-for-longer AI capex cycle, or lower oil prices and interest rates lift confidence in consensus 2028 EPS. At a 19x P/E that gives an S&P 500 of 9,400 at the end of 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: 2028 AI capex is uncertain and rising semiconductor supply threatens margins. If consensus EPS falls to the 30-year trend and the P/E to 17x, the S&P 500 falls about 25% to roughly 5,600.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Consensus S&P 500 EPS estimates falling back to the 30-year trend with the P/E at the 30-year average of 17x.

tension_points.bull_case: Prices imply a substantial decline in EPS over the next few years, which sets a low bar for a short-term bounce.
tension_points.bear_case: Semiconductor earnings and margins run above trend and have fallen more in past downturns, and capex growth and revisions are slowing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Investor confidence in 2028 and later earnings. GS says that visibility is unlikely to arise in the near future, so sustained outperformance is not expected.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue growth accelerated to 54% in Q3 2026, backlogs total $1.8 trillion, and slower capex growth signals better future free cash flow.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex exceeded operating cash flow in Q3 2026 and consensus has free cash flow falling further in 2027, with roughly $3 trillion of lease and purchase commitments.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex slowing because demand is slowing rather than by choice, which GS says would remove the positive read.
